secondary: other: slow stage 0 - the lever (on the toaster's side face) was only fully pressed at ~1011, leaving 320 steps after the pop-up
what_happened: Scene: layout 8, black/silver single-pair toaster turned so that its lever and knob face the robot's right, bread in the left slot. The fingers closed at ~120 and never reopened. Stage 0: 104-560 the gripper hovered over the toaster's slot end and front, touching the housing (245-496) without finding the lever. At ~577-592 it reached the lever face and pushed the lever only to 0.17, then lifted away (620-760). It came back to the lever side at 820-940 and pressed fully at 976-1024 (0.36 -> 1.0; the bread dropped 6.3 cm). Toaster on 1011-1510. The lever rose 1520-1712 and stage 0 completed at 1680 (online log agrees). Stage 1 (320 steps left): the arm swung toward the window/sink 1660-1700, then hovered above the toaster's lever end 1740-2000 with closed fingers. The bread was visible in the wrist view, but the arm never moved over the slot. No bread contact all episode.
causal_chain: ~470 steps searching the toaster before the first, partial lever push (592, 0.17) -> full press only at ~1011 -> pop-up done 1680 -> 320 steps left, spent hovering above the lever end with closed fingers -> no grasp attempt, bread still in the toaster at 2000
self_recovery: After the partial push at 592 the policy came back and pressed fully at ~1011 (stage 0 recovered, late). No attempt at the bread.

packet_facts: gripper closed (0.001) from ~120 to 2000; only close_event 102 (on nothing)

uncertain_about: Whether stage 1 would have gone differently with more time. In the other 7 stage-0-complete episodes, which had 320-1180 steps left, the policy never grasped the bread either, so I put the root cause in stage 1.
